question: In an EU home, which uses the most energy: lights and appliances, hot water, cooking or heating the rooms?
answer: Heating the rooms, about 63% of household energy in the EU, Eurostat reports, with hot water at about 15%. Every light and gadget together comes to about 14%. Heat leaks through walls, windows and roofs all winter, so insulation and the thermostat decide most of the bill, not chargers left in the socket.
move: Before trimming the small switches, find the one that sets most of the bill.
reference: Eurostat (2024) Energy consumption in households, Statistics Explained, data for 2022 (final energy consumption in the residential sector by use)
ask: What is my thermostat set to, and when did anyone last check the loft insulation?

items.label: Appliances
items.note: Fridge, TV, lamps, chargers and the rest together: about a seventh.

items.label: Cooking
items.note: About 6%: the hob and oven matter least.

items.label: Hot water
items.note: As much as every light and appliance together: long showers count.

items.label: Heating
items.note: Nearly two thirds: the thermostat matters more than every switch.
